```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, include = FALSE}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2009_vegf_svegfr1_qsp"))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0005108> (open access,
  PMC2663039). All 61 ODEs are printed in Methods section 2 (Eqs. 7-39); the
  parameter values are in Tables 1-11, with the unit conversions in the table
  footnotes.

Wu 2009 is a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model of the endogenous
vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) system in a healthy 70 kg human. The
body is split into three compartments: a calf compartment (unilateral
gastrocnemius and soleus), a "normal" compartment holding the rest of the
body's tissue, and blood. In each tissue, myocytes secrete VEGF121 and
VEGF165 (1:10), endothelial cells secrete soluble VEGF receptor-1 (sVEGFR1,
also called sFlt-1), and both bind heparan-sulfate sites in the interstitial
matrix and the abluminal endothelial receptors VEGFR1, VEGFR2 and
neuropilin-1 (NRP1). Free VEGF, free sVEGFR1 and their complexes leave the
interstitium by lymph flow and move in both directions across the capillary
wall; in blood they are cleared first order.

There is no drug. The model asks whether sVEGFR1, acting only as a
diffusible VEGF trap, lowers VEGF signalling, and how sensitive plasma VEGF
and sVEGFR1, used clinically as biomarkers, are to physiological changes in
lymph flow and permeability. Nothing is estimated from individual data: the
geometry, kinetics, transport rates and receptor densities come from the
literature, and only the four secretion rates were calibrated so that plasma
free VEGF is 1.5 pM and plasma free sVEGFR1 is 100 pM.

**Units.** The states are concentrations per cm^3 of whole tissue or whole
blood, in pM (the paper's mol/cm^3 multiplied by 10^15). The outputs
(`vegf_free_plasma`, `svegfr1_free_plasma`, `vegf_free_is_norm`, ...) divide
by the available fluid fraction (`kav_*`), so they are concentrations in
plasma or available interstitial fluid, as the paper reports them. Time is in
seconds, as in the paper.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- mod$population
tibble::tibble(Field = names(pop), Value = vapply(pop, paste, character(1), collapse = " ")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The "patient" is a single typical healthy adult: a 70 kg man with 65 kg of
non-blood tissue (treated as skeletal muscle at 1.06 g/cm^3) and 5 L of blood,
60% of it plasma (Methods section 3.1).

# Source trace

| Model element | Source |
|---|---|
| Tissue matrix-site states `ecm`, `ebm`, `pbm` and their VEGF165 / sVEGFR1 complexes | Eqs. 7-15 |
| Surface receptor states `r1`, `r2`, `n1` and their 11 complexes | Eqs. 16-29 |
| Insertion of free receptors `kint * [R_total]` | Methods section 2.1ii ("sR = kint [Rtotal]") |
| Interstitial free VEGF121, VEGF165, sVEGFR1 and VEGF-sVEGFR1 complexes | Eqs. 30-34 |
| Blood states (free VEGF121, VEGF165, sVEGFR1 and the two complexes) | Eqs. 35-39 |
| Conversion to fluid concentrations, `[X]_IS = [X]_j / KAV_j`, `[X]_pl = [X]_B / KAV_B` | Eqs. 1-6 |
| Compartment volumes, available fluid fractions, ESAV | Table 1; Methods section 3.1 |
| Binding, coupling and internalization rate constants (in vivo values) | Table 3 and its footnote |
| Matrix binding-site densities | Table 7 |
| Receptor densities (10,000 per endothelial cell) | Table 8 |
| Vascular permeability and plasma clearance | Table 4 |
| Surface-area recruitment factors | Table 5 |
| Lymph flow (supine awake control, and the other activity levels) | Table 6; Figure 9A footer |
| Secretion rates | Table 11 and its footnote; Results section 1.1 |
| Endothelial surface area per compartment, `S_jB = ESAV_j * U_j` | Methods section 2.1iii definition of S_jB; Table 1 |
| Calibration targets (plasma free VEGF 1.5 pM, sVEGFR1 100 pM) | Tables 9-10 |
| Steady-state distributions used for validation | Results section 1.2; Figures 9A, 10 |
| Diurnal lymph-flow simulation | Results section 6.3; Figure 9C |

# Approach to the healthy steady state

The paper solves the ODEs "as an initial value problem to steady state"
without giving the starting point. The packaged model starts with every
receptor and matrix site free and no ligand anywhere. VEGF settles within
hours; sVEGFR1, whose plasma half-life is about 38 h and which is 97%
matrix-bound in tissue, takes about three months; calf interstitial sVEGFR1
is the slowest output.

```{r equilibrate}
day <- 86400
eq_times <- sort(c(0, 10^seq(1, log10(120 * day), length.out = 120), 90 * day))
ss <- rxSolve(mod, et(eq_times), returnType = "data.frame")

ss |>
  select(time, vegf_free_plasma, svegfr1_free_plasma, vegf_free_is_norm, vegf_free_is_calf,
         svegfr1_free_is_norm, svegfr1_free_is_calf) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / day, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days, log scale)", y = "Free concentration (pM)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Approach to the healthy control steady state")
```

```{r steady-state-check}
ctrl <- ss[nrow(ss), ]
at90 <- ss[ss$time == 90 * day, ]
outs <- c("vegf_free_plasma", "svegfr1_free_plasma", "vegf_free_is_norm",
          "vegf_free_is_calf", "svegfr1_free_is_norm", "svegfr1_free_is_calf")
# Change between day 90 and day 120: the system is at steady state by day 90.
drift <- abs(unlist(at90[outs]) / unlist(ctrl[outs]) - 1)
stopifnot(max(drift) < 1e-3)

paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~output, ~quantity, ~paper,
  "vegf_free_plasma", "Plasma free VEGF (pM)", 1.5,
  "svegfr1_free_plasma", "Plasma free sVEGFR1 (pM)", 100,
  "vegf_free_is_norm", "Interstitial free VEGF, rest of body (pM)", 10,
  "vegf_free_is_calf", "Interstitial free VEGF, calf (pM)", 10,
  "svegfr1_free_is_norm", "Interstitial free sVEGFR1, rest of body (pM)", 36,
  "svegfr1_free_is_calf", "Interstitial free sVEGFR1, calf (pM)", 36
)
ss_tab <- paper |>
  mutate(model = unlist(ctrl[output]), pct_diff = 100 * (model / paper - 1))
ss_tab |>
  select(-output) |>
  rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Wu 2009 (Tables 9-10)" = paper, "Model" = model,
         "% difference" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# Deterministic model; the paper's targets are themselves rounded (10 pM, 36 pM).
stopifnot(all(abs(ss_tab$pct_diff) < 5))
```

## Molecular distribution at the healthy control

Results section 1.2 lists how VEGF, sVEGFR1, the receptors and the matrix
sites are partitioned at the control steady state. The model reproduces every
percentage to within rounding.

```{r distribution}
frac <- function(x, j, num, den) {
  sum(unlist(x[paste0(num, "_", j)])) / sum(unlist(x[paste0(den, "_", j)]))
}
r1_all <- c("r1", "v121_r1", "v165_r1", "r1_n1", "v121_r1_n1")
r2_all <- c("r2", "v121_r2", "v165_r2", "r2_v165_n1")
n1_all <- c("n1", "v121_n1", "v165_n1", "r1_n1", "sr1_n1", "v121_r1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1", "r2_v165_n1")
v121_all <- c("v121", "v121_sr1", "v121_r1", "v121_r2", "v121_n1", "v121_r1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1")
v165_all <- c("v165", "v165_sr1", "v165_r1", "v165_r2", "v165_n1", "r2_v165_n1",
              "v165_ecm", "v165_ebm", "v165_pbm")
sr1_all <- c("sr1", "v121_sr1", "v165_sr1", "sr1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1", "sr1_ecm", "sr1_ebm", "sr1_pbm")

dist_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~j, ~num, ~den, ~paper,
  "VEGFR1 free", "norm", "r1", r1_all, 26,
  "VEGFR1 NRP1-coupled, unligated", "norm", "r1_n1", r1_all, 66,
  "VEGFR1 VEGF-ligated", "norm", c("v121_r1", "v165_r1", "v121_r1_n1"), r1_all, 8,
  "VEGFR2 free", "norm", "r2", r2_all, 80,
  "VEGFR2 VEGF-ligated", "norm", c("v121_r2", "v165_r2", "r2_v165_n1"), r2_all, 20,
  "NRP1 free", "norm", "n1", n1_all, 16,
  "NRP1 coupled to VEGFR1 (unligated)", "norm", "r1_n1", n1_all, 66,
  "NRP1 in signalling complexes", "norm", c("v121_r1_n1", "r2_v165_n1"), n1_all, 18,
  "VEGF121 free, rest of body", "norm", "v121", v121_all, 0.9,
  "VEGF121 sVEGFR1-bound, rest of body", "norm", "v121_sr1", v121_all, 0.8,
  "VEGF121 receptor-bound, rest of body", "norm",
  c("v121_r1", "v121_r2", "v121_n1", "v121_r1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1"), v121_all, 98.3,
  "VEGF165 free, rest of body", "norm", "v165", v165_all, 0.6,
  "VEGF165 receptor-bound, rest of body", "norm",
  c("v165_r1", "v165_r2", "v165_n1", "r2_v165_n1"), v165_all, 63.0,
  "VEGF165 matrix-bound, rest of body", "norm", c("v165_ecm", "v165_ebm", "v165_pbm"), v165_all, 35.8,
  "VEGF121 free, calf", "calf", "v121", v121_all, 4.8,
  "VEGF121 sVEGFR1-bound, calf", "calf", "v121_sr1", v121_all, 5.0,
  "VEGF121 receptor-bound, calf", "calf",
  c("v121_r1", "v121_r2", "v121_n1", "v121_r1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1"), v121_all, 90.2,
  "VEGF165 free, calf", "calf", "v165", v165_all, 1.4,
  "VEGF165 receptor-bound, calf", "calf",
  c("v165_r1", "v165_r2", "v165_n1", "r2_v165_n1"), v165_all, 24.7,
  "VEGF165 matrix-bound, calf", "calf", c("v165_ecm", "v165_ebm", "v165_pbm"), v165_all, 72.4,
  "sVEGFR1 free, rest of body", "norm", "sr1", sr1_all, 1.6,
  "sVEGFR1 matrix-bound, rest of body", "norm", c("sr1_ecm", "sr1_ebm", "sr1_pbm"), sr1_all, 97.4,
  "sVEGFR1 free, calf", "calf", "sr1", sr1_all, 1.9,
  "sVEGFR1 matrix-bound, calf", "calf", c("sr1_ecm", "sr1_ebm", "sr1_pbm"), sr1_all, 97.4
)
dist_tab$model <- 100 * mapply(frac, j = dist_tab$j, num = dist_tab$num, den = dist_tab$den,
                               MoreArgs = list(x = ctrl))

plasma_vegf_tot <- with(ctrl, v121_blood + v165_blood + v121_sr1_blood + v165_sr1_blood)
plasma_sr1_tot <- with(ctrl, sr1_blood + v121_sr1_blood + v165_sr1_blood)
plasma_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("Plasma VEGF free (of total VEGF)", "Plasma sVEGFR1 free (of total sVEGFR1)"),
  paper = c(23, 95),
  model = 100 * c(with(ctrl, v121_blood + v165_blood) / plasma_vegf_tot,
                  ctrl$sr1_blood / plasma_sr1_tot)
)
dist_all <- bind_rows(select(dist_tab, quantity, paper, model), plasma_tab) |>
  mutate(diff = model - paper)
dist_all |>
  rename("Quantity (% of total)" = quantity, "Wu 2009 (Results 1.2)" = paper, "Model" = model,
         "Difference (points)" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# The paper rounds to whole percentages for the receptors and to 0.1% for the
# ligand pools.
stopifnot(all(abs(dist_all$diff) < 1))
```

The isoform ratios are also reproduced: free VEGF121:VEGF165 is
1:`r round(ctrl$v165_blood / ctrl$v121_blood, 1)` in plasma (paper 1:10.8)
and 1:`r round(ctrl$v165_norm / ctrl$v121_norm, 1)` in the interstitium
(paper 1:10.6).

## Mass balance

At steady state, everything secreted must leave either by internalization
of a receptor complex or by clearance from plasma. Lymph flow and vascular
permeability only move mass between compartments, so this checks that the
transport terms were written with consistent volumes.

```{r mass-balance}
th <- mod$theta
vols <- c(norm = th[["vol_norm"]], calf = th[["vol_calf"]])
internalized <- function(species) {
  sum(vapply(names(vols), function(j) {
    th[["kint_bound"]] * vols[[j]] * sum(unlist(ctrl[paste0(species, "_", j)]))
  }, numeric(1)))
}
vegf_in <- sum(vapply(names(vols), function(j) {
  (th[[paste0("ksyn_v121_", j)]] + th[[paste0("ksyn_v165_", j)]]) * vols[[j]]
}, numeric(1)))
vegf_out <- internalized(c("v121_r1", "v121_r2", "v121_n1", "v165_r1", "v165_r2", "v165_n1",
                           "v121_r1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1", "r2_v165_n1")) +
  th[["vol_blood"]] * (th[["kcl_v"]] * (ctrl$v121_blood + ctrl$v165_blood) +
                         th[["kcl_v_sr1"]] * (ctrl$v121_sr1_blood + ctrl$v165_sr1_blood))
sr1_in <- sum(vapply(names(vols), function(j) th[[paste0("ksyn_sr1_", j)]] * vols[[j]], numeric(1)))
sr1_out <- internalized(c("sr1_n1", "v121_sr1_n1")) +
  th[["vol_blood"]] * (th[["kcl_sr1"]] * ctrl$sr1_blood +
                         th[["kcl_v_sr1"]] * (ctrl$v121_sr1_blood + ctrl$v165_sr1_blood))
mb <- tibble::tibble(
  Species = c("VEGF", "sVEGFR1"),
  "Secretion (fmol/s)" = c(vegf_in, sr1_in),
  "Internalization + clearance (fmol/s)" = c(vegf_out, sr1_out)
)
knitr::kable(mb, digits = 4)
stopifnot(abs(vegf_out / vegf_in - 1) < 1e-3, abs(sr1_out / sr1_in - 1) < 1e-3)
```

Of the `r round(vegf_in, 1)` fmol/s of VEGF secreted,
`r round(100 * th[["vol_blood"]] * th[["kcl_v"]] * (ctrl$v121_blood + ctrl$v165_blood) / vegf_in, 2)`%
is cleared from plasma as free VEGF; almost all of the rest is internalized
in the tissue where it was secreted, the point the paper's flow diagram
(Figure 4) makes.

# Secretion-rate calibration (Figures 2 and 3)

Results section 1.1 describes how the secretion rates were chosen. Without
sVEGFR1, total VEGF secretion of (0.264, 0.154) molecules/MD/s from
(rest of body, calf) gives plasma VEGF 1.5 pM and interstitial VEGF 15 pM.
Adding sVEGFR1 at those VEGF rates raises plasma VEGF to 2.1 pM, so VEGF
secretion was lowered to (0.1925, 0.1155) molecules/MD/s, which gives plasma
VEGF 1 pM without sVEGFR1. The conversions to pM/s use the Table 11 footnote
factors (4.82 and 4.96 x 10^-17 mol/cm^3/s per molecule/MD/s).

```{r secretion}
q_pms <- function(total_norm, total_calf) {
  c(ksyn_v121_norm = total_norm / 11 * 4.82e-17 * 1e15,
    ksyn_v165_norm = 10 * total_norm / 11 * 4.82e-17 * 1e15,
    ksyn_v121_calf = total_calf / 11 * 4.96e-17 * 1e15,
    ksyn_v165_calf = 10 * total_calf / 11 * 4.96e-17 * 1e15)
}
sec_par <- as.data.frame(rbind(
  c(id = 1, q_pms(0.1925, 0.1155), ksyn_sr1_norm = 0, ksyn_sr1_calf = 0),
  c(id = 2, q_pms(0.264, 0.154), ksyn_sr1_norm = 0, ksyn_sr1_calf = 0),
  c(id = 3, q_pms(0.264, 0.154), ksyn_sr1_norm = th[["ksyn_sr1_norm"]],
    ksyn_sr1_calf = th[["ksyn_sr1_calf"]])
))
sec <- rxSolve(mod, et(c(0, 120 * day)) |> et(id = 1:3), params = sec_par,
               returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time == 120 * day)
sec_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Scenario = c("Calibrated VEGF secretion, no sVEGFR1",
               "Initial VEGF secretion, no sVEGFR1",
               "Initial VEGF secretion, control sVEGFR1 secretion"),
  "Plasma VEGF, paper (pM)" = c(1, 1.5, 2.1),
  "Plasma VEGF, model (pM)" = sec$vegf_free_plasma,
  "Interstitial VEGF rest of body, model (pM)" = sec$vegf_free_is_norm,
  "Interstitial VEGF calf, model (pM)" = sec$vegf_free_is_calf,
  "Plasma sVEGFR1, model (pM)" = sec$svegfr1_free_plasma
)
knitr::kable(sec_tab, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  abs(sec$vegf_free_plasma[1] / 1 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(sec$vegf_free_plasma[2] / 1.5 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(sec$vegf_free_is_norm[2] / 15 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(sec$vegf_free_plasma[3] / 2.1 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

The third row is `r round(sec$vegf_free_plasma[3], 2)` pM rather than
2.1 pM because the paper adjusted sVEGFR1 secretion to give 100 pM plasma
sVEGFR1 at the higher VEGF secretion, while this scenario keeps the final
control sVEGFR1 secretion (plasma sVEGFR1
`r round(sec$svegfr1_free_plasma[3])` pM). The comparison shows the paper's
counter-intuitive result: adding sVEGFR1 raises plasma VEGF while leaving
interstitial VEGF almost unchanged.

# Steady-state sensitivity to lymph flow and plasma clearance (Figures 9A and 10)

Figure 9A varies the lymph flow rate of both tissues over the activity
levels in Table 6, and Figure 10 scales the plasma clearance of all three
soluble species 0.1-fold and 10-fold. Each scenario is solved to steady state
(120 days).

```{r sensitivity}
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~klymph_norm, ~klymph_calf, ~kcl_fold, ~paper_vegf_free_pct, ~paper_sr1_free_pct,
  "Low", 0.014, 0.00026, 1, 35, 97,
  "Night", 0.028, 0.0005, 1, 33, 97,
  "Control", 0.14, 0.0026, 1, 23, 95,
  "Steady exercise", 0.28, 0.0051, 1, 18, 94,
  "Calf peak exercise", 0.28, 0.013, 1, 18, 94,
  "Peak exercise", 0.7, 0.013, 1, 13, 91,
  "High", 1.4, 0.026, 1, 10, 86,
  "kCL x 0.1", 0.14, 0.0026, 0.1, 21, 81,
  "kCL x 10", 0.14, 0.0026, 10, 21, 98
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
sens_par <- scen |>
  transmute(id, klymph_norm, klymph_calf,
            kcl_v = th[["kcl_v"]] * kcl_fold,
            kcl_sr1 = th[["kcl_sr1"]] * kcl_fold,
            kcl_v_sr1 = th[["kcl_v_sr1"]] * kcl_fold)
sens <- rxSolve(mod, et(c(0, 120 * day)) |> et(id = scen$id), params = as.data.frame(sens_par),
                returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time == 120 * day) |>
  mutate(
    vegf_free_pct = 100 * (v121_blood + v165_blood) /
      (v121_blood + v165_blood + v121_sr1_blood + v165_sr1_blood),
    sr1_free_pct = 100 * sr1_blood / (sr1_blood + v121_sr1_blood + v165_sr1_blood)
  ) |>
  left_join(scen, by = "id")

sens |>
  select(scenario, vegf_free_plasma, vegf_free_pct, paper_vegf_free_pct,
         svegfr1_free_plasma, sr1_free_pct, paper_sr1_free_pct,
         svegfr1_free_is_norm, svegfr1_free_is_calf) |>
  rename("Scenario" = scenario,
         "Plasma VEGF (pM)" = vegf_free_plasma,
         "VEGF free, % (model)" = vegf_free_pct,
         "VEGF free, % (paper)" = paper_vegf_free_pct,
         "Plasma sVEGFR1 (pM)" = svegfr1_free_plasma,
         "sVEGFR1 free, % (model)" = sr1_free_pct,
         "sVEGFR1 free, % (paper)" = paper_sr1_free_pct,
         "IS sVEGFR1 rest of body (pM)" = svegfr1_free_is_norm,
         "IS sVEGFR1 calf (pM)" = svegfr1_free_is_calf) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# The paper's figure labels are whole percentages.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(sens$vegf_free_pct - sens$paper_vegf_free_pct) < 1.5),
  all(abs(sens$sr1_free_pct - sens$paper_sr1_free_pct) < 1.5)
)
```

Results section 6.2 states that over the physiological lymph-flow range
(night to whole-body peak exercise) plasma sVEGFR1 and VEGF "could vary up to
164 pM and 2.4 pM respectively".

```{r kl-range}
phys <- sens |> filter(scenario %in% c("Night", "Peak exercise"))
range_sr1 <- diff(phys$svegfr1_free_plasma)
range_vegf <- diff(phys$vegf_free_plasma)
c(sVEGFR1_range_pM = range_sr1, VEGF_range_pM = range_vegf)
stopifnot(abs(range_sr1 / 164 - 1) < 0.03, abs(range_vegf / 2.4 - 1) < 0.03)
```

```{r sensitivity-plot, fig.height = 5}
sens |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scen$scenario)) |>
  select(scenario, vegf_free_plasma, vegf_free_is_norm, vegf_free_is_calf,
         svegfr1_free_plasma, svegfr1_free_is_norm, svegfr1_free_is_calf) |>
  pivot_longer(-scenario) |>
  mutate(
    molecule = ifelse(grepl("^vegf", name), "Free VEGF", "Free sVEGFR1"),
    where = case_when(
      grepl("plasma", name) ~ "Plasma",
      grepl("norm", name) ~ "Rest-of-body interstitium",
      TRUE ~ "Calf interstitium"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(scenario, value, colour = where, shape = where)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~molecule, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Concentration (pM)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       title = "Steady-state sensitivity to lymph flow and plasma clearance",
       caption = "Replicates Figures 9A and 10 of Wu 2009.") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
```

As the paper reports, lymph flow and plasma clearance move the plasma
concentrations of both markers several-fold, while interstitial free VEGF,
and with it VEGF receptor occupancy, barely changes.

# Diurnal lymph flow (Figure 9C)

Figure 9C follows a week of daily cycles: 15 h awake followed by 9 h asleep
(night lymph flow). Days 1, 2 and 4 are bed-rest days (awake lymph flow at the
control rate); days 3, 5 and 6 are active days, which start with a peak in lymph
flow at the peak-exercise rate and settle to the steady-exercise rate; day 7
raises lymph flow only in the calf. The paper does not state how long the
early-exercise peak lasts; this simulation uses 1 h, matching the
"peak ... at 1 h post-onset of exercise" in Methods section 3.3ii.

Lymph flow is passed as time-varying data columns (`klymph_norm`,
`klymph_calf`). The 120-day equilibration at control runs in the same solve,
so the week starts from the healthy steady state.

```{r diurnal}
teq <- 120 * day
hr <- seq(0, 168, by = 0.1)
day_type <- c("bed", "bed", "active", "bed", "active", "active", "calf")[pmin(floor(hr / 24) + 1, 7)]
hod <- hr %% 24
awake <- hod < 15
peak <- hod < 1
klym_norm <- ifelse(!awake, 0.028, ifelse(day_type == "active", ifelse(peak, 0.7, 0.28), 0.14))
klym_calf <- ifelse(!awake, 0.0005,
                    ifelse(day_type %in% c("active", "calf"), ifelse(peak, 0.013, 0.0051), 0.0026))
eq_grid <- c(0, 10^seq(0, log10(teq), length.out = 40))
eq_grid <- eq_grid[eq_grid < teq]
ev_week <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = eq_grid, evid = 0, cmt = "sr1_blood",
             klymph_norm = 0.14, klymph_calf = 0.0026),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = teq + hr * 3600, evid = 0, cmt = "sr1_blood",
             klymph_norm = klym_norm, klymph_calf = klym_calf)
)
week <- rxSolve(mod, ev_week, returnType = "data.frame", covsInterpolation = "locf") |>
  mutate(hr = time / 3600 - teq / 3600) |>
  filter(hr >= 0)
```

```{r diurnal-plot, fig.height = 5}
week |>
  select(hr, "Free sVEGFR1, plasma" = svegfr1_free_plasma,
         "sVEGFR1-VEGF, plasma" = vegf_svegfr1_plasma,
         "Free VEGF, plasma" = vegf_free_plasma,
         "Free sVEGFR1, rest-of-body IS" = svegfr1_free_is_norm,
         "Free sVEGFR1, calf IS" = svegfr1_free_is_calf) |>
  pivot_longer(-hr) |>
  ggplot(aes(hr, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ grepl("VEGF, plasma|sVEGFR1-VEGF", name), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(`FALSE` = "sVEGFR1 (pM)", `TRUE` = "VEGF and complex (pM)"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, by = 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Bed-rest days 1, 2, 4; active days 3, 5, 6; calf-only activity day 7",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 9C of Wu 2009.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

```{r diurnal-check}
base_sr1 <- week$svegfr1_free_plasma[1]
base_vegf <- week$vegf_free_plasma[1]
win <- function(lo, hi) week$hr >= lo - 1e-6 & week$hr <= hi + 1e-6
at <- function(h) which.min(abs(week$hr - h))
dyn <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~paper,
  "Plasma sVEGFR1 rise during the first active day (pM)", 42,
  "Plasma sVEGFR1 rise during the second consecutive active day (pM)", 44,
  "Plasma sVEGFR1 change after sleep following a bed-rest day (pM)", -32,
  "Plasma sVEGFR1 change after sleep following an active day (pM)", -16,
  "Range of plasma sVEGFR1 over the week (pM)", 76,
  "Range of interstitial sVEGFR1, rest of body (pM)", 2.5,
  "Plasma VEGF rise during the first active day (pM)", 1.1,
  "Plasma VEGF rise during the second consecutive active day (pM)", 1.0,
  "Range of plasma VEGF over the week (pM)", 1.65,
  "Range of interstitial VEGF, calf (pM)", 0.2
)
dyn$model <- c(
  max(week$svegfr1_free_plasma[win(48, 63)]) - base_sr1,
  max(week$svegfr1_free_plasma[win(120, 135)]) - base_sr1,
  week$svegfr1_free_plasma[at(24)] - base_sr1,
  week$svegfr1_free_plasma[at(72)] - base_sr1,
  diff(range(week$svegfr1_free_plasma)),
  diff(range(week$svegfr1_free_is_norm)),
  max(week$vegf_free_plasma[win(48, 63)]) - base_vegf,
  max(week$vegf_free_plasma[win(120, 135)]) - base_vegf,
  diff(range(week$vegf_free_plasma)),
  diff(range(week$vegf_free_is_calf))
)
dyn |>
  rename("Quantity (Results 6.3)" = quantity, "Wu 2009" = paper, "Model" = model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# sVEGFR1 responds over hours and does not depend on the unstated shape of the
# exercise peak; these are compared tightly.
stopifnot(all(abs(dyn$model[1:5] / dyn$paper[1:5] - 1) < 0.1),
          abs(dyn$model[6] / dyn$paper[6] - 1) < 0.15)
```

The sVEGFR1 response matches the paper closely: activity raises plasma
sVEGFR1 by about 43 pM over 15 h, and one night's sleep brings it below
control. The VEGF peaks are higher than the paper's (about 1.5 pM rather than
1.1 pM above control). Plasma VEGF settles within minutes, so its peak
follows the peak lymph flow, whose duration and shape the paper does not give.
The plateau during steady exercise
(`r round(week$vegf_free_plasma[at(62)] - base_vegf, 2)` pM above control)
and the night-time fall are as described.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Table 11 misprint (calf VEGF165 secretion).** Table 11 prints the calf
  VEGF165 secretion rate as 2.73 x 10^-18 mol/cm^3/s. Three other statements
  in the paper give 5.21 x 10^-18: 0.105 molecules/MD/s times the Table 11
  footnote factor 4.96 x 10^-17; the 1:10 VEGF121:VEGF165 ratio applied to the
  calf VEGF121 rate (5.21 x 10^-19); and the total calf VEGF secretion of
  5.7 x 10^-18 mol/cm^3/s in Results section 1.1. The model uses 5.21 x 10^-18.
  With it, calf interstitial VEGF is 10.4 pM, in line with the paper's
  "10 pM" in both tissues; the printed value would roughly halve it.
* **Endothelial surface area `S_jB`.** The paper defines `S_jB` as the total
  abluminal endothelial surface area of tissue j but gives no number. The
  model uses `ESAV_j * U_j` from Table 1 (4.41 x 10^6 cm^2 for the rest of the
  body, 3.82 x 10^4 cm^2 for the calf). The reproduction of the calibration
  targets, which depend directly on vascular permeability, supports this
  reading.
* **Initial conditions.** Not stated in the paper. The model starts with all
  receptors and matrix sites free and no ligand. The receptor and matrix-site
  totals are conserved, so the steady state does not depend on this choice.
  The `x(0)` assignments in the model take precedence over `inits`, so to
  start a perturbation from the healthy steady state, keep an equilibration
  period of at least 90 days in the same solve, as done above.
* **Available fluid fractions.** The model uses the rounded 3% and 11% of
  Table 1, the values behind every in vivo rate constant in Table 3.
* **Internalization and insertion.** The paper sets one internalization rate
  for free receptors and one for complexes (both 2.8 x 10^-4 1/s) and inserts
  free receptors at `kint * [R_total]`. The model keeps the two rates
  separate (`kint_free`, `kint_bound`); total receptor density is conserved
  only while they are equal.
* **VEGF121-NRP1 binding** is off in the base case (`kon` and `koff` = 0,
  Table 3), so the `v121_n1_*` states stay at zero. The paper's sensitivity
  analysis switches it on by setting `kon_v121_n1_*` and `koff_v121_n1`.
* **Matrix-site densities.** The caption of Figure 7 gives the control
  densities as "[ECM] = 20 uM; [BM] = 0.75 uM", the reverse of Table 7
  (ECM 0.75 uM, basement membranes 20 uM). The model follows Table 7, whose
  per-tissue values (e.g. 2.15 x 10^-11 mol/cm^3 for the rest-of-body ECM
  = 0.75 uM x 2.87 x 10^-5) agree with its own conversion footnote.
* **Blood binding.** Table 3 also lists blood-phase rate constants for
  sVEGFR1 binding to matrix sites and NRP1, but the blood equations (Eqs.
  35-39) contain no matrix sites or receptors, so only the blood VEGF-sVEGFR1
  association is used.
* **Plasma clearance scenarios (Figure 10).** The paper says only that kCL was
  varied 0.1- and 10-fold; the vignette scales the clearance of free VEGF,
  free sVEGFR1 and the complex together.
* **Diurnal schedule (Figure 9C).** The bed-rest, active and calf-only days
  follow the figure, with the activity-level lymph flows of Table 6 and Figure
  9A. The 1 h duration of the early-exercise lymph-flow peak is an assumption,
  and it affects only the height of the plasma VEGF peaks.
* **No IIV or residual error.** The paper describes one typical healthy
  subject; the model is deterministic.
* **Errata.** No erratum to the article was found (PLOS ONE article page and
  PubMed, checked 2026-11-19).
